newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Family of five killed by Burundi rebels -- radio.
newsitem.headline: Family of five killed by Burundi rebels -- radio.

text.p: Hutu rebels have killed a family of five ethnic Tutsis in Burundi's eastern Ruyigi region shortly after they returned to their home from a camp for displaced persons, state radio reported on Sunday.
The rebels attacked the family, displaced during fighting in 1993, at their home in Ruyigi town on Saturday night, the radio said.
"They were people who were displaced in 1993 in the war and they had just returned to their homes when the assailants (rebels) came and killed them," the radio said. It gave no further details.

Ruyigi region, close to the Tanzanian border, has been relatively free from ethnic violence in recent months, while rebels have staged a series of attacks in northern Kayanza, Ngozi and Karuzi regions.

Rebels for three days battled the Tutsi-dominated army in the hills surrounding Bujumbura last week in what the main rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), described as a show of strength.

The rebels have stepped up their attacks since military strongman Pierre Buyoya came to power in an army coup on July 25, ousting a Hutu president, Sylvestre Ntibantunganya -- who is still holed up in the U.S. Embassy, where he took refuge.
Around 150,000 people have died in the civil war in Burundi since October 1993, when the country's first democratically-elected president, a Hutu, was assassinated in an attempted coup.
